2608.20786.title: Structure for Reading, Prose for Writing: Asymmetric Structural Conditioning in Multi-Agent Document Authoring
2608.20786.paper_summary: Multi-agent pipelines that author formal documents must both read a requester's forms and write against them. We report a deployed tender-response system, running an open-weights model under sovereignty constraints, and evaluate it against human-written bids the same organisation actually submitted. On a blind comparison where the system had no worked example available, an LLM judge rated its answers at least as good as the human-submitted answer on $40$ of $55$ ground-truth sections, better on $4$, missing on none, and flagged one unsupported claim in total. Classifying every gap the judge identified shows that $68\%$ were content absent from the system's own sources -- knowledge the human author held and the pipeline was never given -- so only $6$ of the $15$ adverse verdicts involve a deficiency the system could have avoided. A divergence from ground truth is more often an information-availability result than a writing-quality one, and evaluations that do not separate the two understate such systems. Against this backdrop we report a conditioning asymmetry. It is well established that rendering documents as structural markup rather than flat prose improves extraction, and we reproduce that on three reading tasks. The benefit does not transfer to conditioning: converting a bid's \emph{instruction} material from prose to nested XML dropped answer quality from $74\%$ to $48\%$ under a paired comparison. We further find that naming a forbidden construction concentrates rather than removes it -- $96\%$ of surviving defects fall in the two forms the prompt explicitly names -- and that coupling a stochastic annotation to a deterministic windowing function moves the extracted requirement count from $68$ to $51$ on a byte-identical file. Structure belongs where the model reads; prose and self-applied tests belong where it writes.
2608.20786.paper_summary_zh: 多代理管道在撰寫正式文件時必須同時閱讀請求者的表單並根據它們進行寫作。我們報告了一個已部署的投標回應系統，在主權限制下運行開放權重模型，並將其與該組織實際提交的人類撰寫的投標進行評估。在一個盲比較中，系統沒有可用的工作範例，一位 LLM 評審將其答案評價為至少與人類提交的答案一樣好，在 $55$ 個真實部分中有 $40$ 個部分表現良好，$4$ 個部分表現更佳，沒有漏掉任何部分，並總共標記了一個不支持的主張。對評審所識別的每一個缺口進行分類顯示，$68\%$ 的內容來自系統自身來源的缺失——這是人類作者擁有的知識，而管道從未獲得——因此 $15$ 個不利判決中只有 $6$ 個涉及系統本可以避免的缺陷。與真實情況的偏差更常是信息可用性的結果，而非寫作質量的問題，而未能將兩者分開的評估低估了這類系統。在這樣的背景下，我們報告了一種條件不對稱性。已經證實，將文檔呈現為結構標記而非平面散文可以改善提取，我們在三個閱讀任務中重現了這一點。這一好處並未轉移到條件化上：將投標的 \emph{指示} 材料從散文轉換為嵌套 XML，使答案質量從 $74\%$ 降至 $48\%$，在配對比較下進行。 我們進一步發現，命名一個禁止的結構會集中而不是消除它——$96\%$ 的存活缺陷落在提示明確命名的兩種形式中——並且將隨機註釋與確定性窗口函數結合，將提取的要求數量從 $68$ 移動到 $51$，在一個字節完全相同的文件上。結構屬於模型閱讀的地方；散文和自我應用的測試屬於模型寫作的地方。
